title: Initial transport marginal
instructions: Return the probability mass assigned to each initial support point s0, sorted ascending by s0.
hint: Work inside out. Collect transport couplings sharing the same first-period support point.

explanation.meaning: Collect transport couplings sharing the same first-period support point.
Marginalize over all destination states s1.
Put source support in increasing price order.

title: Terminal transport marginal
instructions: Return terminal probability masses indexed by s1, sorted by increasing terminal support price.
hint: Work inside out. Collect all flows arriving at each terminal support price.

explanation.meaning: Collect all flows arriving at each terminal support price.
Integrate out the source support s0.

title: Transport-plan option price
instructions: Return the scalar expected payoff under the joint transport mass.
hint: Work inside out. Weight each scenario payoff by joint probability of that source-destination pair.

explanation.meaning: Weight each scenario payoff by joint probability of that source-destination pair.
Integrate over the discrete coupling to obtain the expected payoff.

title: Coupling matrix
instructions: Return a matrix with s0 as rows, s1 as columns and mass as each coupling cell, sorted on both support axes.
hint: Work inside out. Turn long (source,destination,mass) records into a probability matrix.

explanation.meaning: Turn long (source,destination,mass) records into a probability matrix.
Order both supports numerically; matrix row and column sums recover the marginals.

title: Conditional terminal expectation
instructions: For every s0, calculate E[S1 | S0=s0] under the (possibly nonmartingale) coupling as a Series.
hint: Work inside out. Compute the weighted terminal contribution for every coupling cell.

explanation.meaning: Compute the weighted terminal contribution for every coupling cell.
Create numerator and row-marginal denominator for each source support point.
Calculate conditional expectation. Compare with s0 to diagnose martingale violation.

title: Martingale constraint residual
instructions: Return the weighted martingale residual per source support: sum(mass*(s1-s0)) grouped by s0.
hint: Work inside out. Compute the price change associated with each coupling pair.

explanation.meaning: Compute the price change associated with each coupling pair.
Weight each move by its joint probability.
Check the martingale constraint for every initial support; target residual is zero in a true martingale coupling.

title: Negative coupling diagnosis
instructions: Return the scalar total magnitude of negative probability entries (should be zero for this valid synthetic mass).
hint: Work inside out. Keep only negative values and replace positive masses by zero.

explanation.meaning: Keep only negative values and replace positive masses by zero.
Sum the magnitude of invalid negative probability, yielding a scalar diagnostic.

title: Normalize expected transport payoff
instructions: Return expected payoff per unit of total joint mass as a scalar, guarding against rounding of mass.
hint: Work inside out. Compute total probability-weighted payoff.

explanation.meaning: Compute total probability-weighted payoff.
Measure total stored mass, which can differ minutely from 1 after rounding.
Return normalized expectation.

title: Monte Carlo terminal simple returns
instructions: Return terminal price divided by initial price minus one, for each simulated path.
hint: Work inside out. Extract terminal and starting price from every simulated path as two 1D vectors.

explanation.meaning: Extract terminal and starting price from every simulated path as two 1D vectors.
Calculate path-level simple total returns.

title: Per-path maximum drawdown
instructions: Return the maximum drawdown per simulation path as a negative-valued 1D array.
hint: Work inside out. Compute running peak within EACH simulated path, from left to right across time.

explanation.meaning: Compute running peak within EACH simulated path, from left to right across time.
Find drawdown at every path-time cell.
Take the worst drawdown for each path.

title: Arithmetic Asian call payoff
instructions: For each simulated path, return max(average price across time - {strike}, 0) as a 1D array.
hint: Work inside out. Collapse the time axis into one average price per simulated path.

explanation.meaning: Collapse the time axis into one average price per simulated path.
Compute average-price intrinsic value.
Apply the call option payoff floor.

title: Barrier first-passage indicator
instructions: Return a Boolean vector indicating which simulated paths EVER traded at or above {barrier}.
hint: Work inside out. Create a Boolean matrix showing when each path crosses the barrier.

explanation.meaning: Create a Boolean matrix showing when each path crosses the barrier.
Reduce across time, producing one Boolean flag per simulated path.

title: Simulated log-return increments
instructions: Return a matrix of adjacent log-price increments for all paths.
hint: Work inside out. Convert simulated positive prices to log prices.

explanation.meaning: Convert simulated positive prices to log prices.
Subtract adjacent time points within each path, yielding one fewer time column.

title: Cross-path tail wealth
instructions: Normalize every simulated path by its starting price, then return the 10th percentile normalized wealth at each time step.
hint: Work inside out. Extract the starting price of each path while retaining a second dimension for broadcasting.

explanation.meaning: Extract the starting price of each path while retaining a second dimension for broadcasting.
Normalize path prices within each row, producing wealth starting at 1.
Collapse the path axis and return a 1D tail-wealth curve across time.

title: Trapezoidal path-average payoff
instructions: For each path, compute the time average by trapezoidal integration over equally spaced steps, then return max(average-100,0).
hint: Work inside out. Pair each adjacent price on every path; this creates trapezoid endpoint sums.

explanation.meaning: Pair each adjacent price on every path; this creates trapezoid endpoint sums.
Compute equal-time-step trapezoidal average over all intervals, with endpoint weights half of interior weights.
Apply the arithmetic Asian call payoff.

title: Conditional probability matrix
instructions: Return the transport coupling probability matrix normalized by each source-state row marginal, indexed by source and terminal supports.
hint: Work inside out. Turn coupling records into source-by-destination joint mass.

explanation.meaning: Turn coupling records into source-by-destination joint mass.
Compute each source marginal probability.
Divide each row by its own marginal to get conditional terminal probabilities; each row sums to 1.
